curriculumAlignmentSummary: The unit covers digital literacy, information collection (books, web sources, surveys, Google forms), components of digital literacy (digital search, technical skills, communication, collaboration, content creation, ethics), key ideas extraction, poster/billboard designing, and social media tools (YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Podcast, X/Twitter). The supplied model and annual papers focus on programming, C language, HTML, logic gates, and basic computer science concepts from other units, containing no specific items addressing Unit 7 Digital Literacy.

mappings.textbookExerciseCue: Q1.1: Which term is used for the ability to effectively use digital technologies to access information, evaluate it and convert it into meaningful and appealing format?
mappings.controlledTransformation: Recall textbook definition of digital literacy.
mappings.studentPreparationFocus: Memorize core definitions of digital literacy and related competencies.
mappings.textbookEvidenceQuote: Digital literacy is the ability to create information in a digital environment. It refers to the ability to effectively use digital technologies to access information, evaluate it and convert it into meaningful and appealing ways.
mappings.caution: The active textbook covers digital literacy extensively, but past/model papers provided do not contain items matching this unit.

unsupportedPastPaperForms: Logic gates and Boolean algebra simplification
analysisLimits: The supplied model and past papers from 2022-2025 exclusively test programming, C syntax, HTML, flowcharts, and hardware/OS concepts from other units of the grade 10 computer science curriculum.
No questions concerning digital literacy, poster/billboard design, or social media platform features appear in the available exam papers.
